mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS decreases and positive S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in the last month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past two months signals strengthening demand in the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the periods following sustained HOUST increases, or if the correlation between HOUST increases and positive S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the last two months indicates supply-side constraints, which historically correlate with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals a tightening monetary policy with high inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: high inflation with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances, or if the interaction effect between high FEDFUNDS and increasing CPIAUCSL on negative S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in the last month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000 in 1 month
regime_hint: tight labor market with strong job growth
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the interaction effect between low UNRATE and increasing PAYEMS on positive S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the past two months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of the periods following sustained RSAFS increases, or if the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is growing at a rate below 1% annually and GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% annually, it signals a weak supply-side environment with sluggish economic growth, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO growth < 1% annually and GDPC1 growth < 2% annually
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances, or if the interaction effect between slow INDPRO growth and slow GDPC1 growth on negative S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
